subject.title: fix(browser): prove post-action target continuity before adopting a tab

question: After a current-main rebase, should browser owners accept stale acted-on target IDs as the required fail-safe outcome whenever a backend cannot prove continuity, rather than preserving heuristic recovery to a surviving tab?
rationale: This is an intentional compatibility and session-continuity contract change: source and proof support the safety rationale, but maintainers must accept the recovery behavior for existing browser-control callers.

options.title: Accept fail-safe target semantics
options.body: Rebase and land after final-head checks confirm routes return only backend-owned or stale acted-on IDs and never infer an unrelated replacement.

options.title: Require an explicit recovery contract
options.body: Keep the PR open until browser owners define and validate an alternate supported recovery mechanism for callers that need continuation after target replacement.

recommendation.title: Accept fail-safe target semantics
recommendation.body: Rebase and land after final-head checks confirm routes return only backend-owned or stale acted-on IDs and never infer an unrelated replacement.

likelyOwner.reason: The canonical report supplies the target-identity contract and explicitly calls for browser-contract review.
